name: Monitor Process State
description: Adversaries may gather information about the physical process state. This information may be used to gain more information about the process itself or used as a trigger for malicious actions. The sources of process state information may vary such as, OPC tags, historian data, specific PLC block information, or network traffic.

telemetry.name: Application Log Content
telemetry.description: Application-emitted audit or operational event content.
telemetry.collection_focus: Select the application event family required by the detection and document its native schema before normalization.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

telemetry.name: Network Connection Creation
telemetry.description: Creation of an endpoint network connection linked to a process.
telemetry.collection_focus: Enable scoped Sysmon NetworkConnect (3), disabled by default, or a platform-equivalent process-aware network sensor.

providers.name: Microsoft Sysmon
providers.scope: Windows event-based collection; enable the event types needed below.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: Linux alternative for supported system-call and file events; different semantics and fields.

providers.name: Apple Endpoint Security clients
providers.scope: macOS alternative where the subscribed event exists; requires an entitled, approved client, not an iOS collector.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Event filtering and sensor versions change coverage. High-volume image-load and process-access collection needs tuning; endpoint events alone do not establish intent.

sources.title: Apple Endpoint Security framework for macOS

telemetry.anomaly_design: Per host role and user: rare process/object combinations, bursts of object access or modification, and ordered parent/action sequences. Compare maintenance windows and signed software rollout activity.

telemetry.name: Network Traffic Content
telemetry.description: Packet or decoded application-protocol content visible at a network sensor.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope approved packet capture/protocol content collection to the lab flow; retain capture provenance and truncation indicators.

providers.name: Zeek
providers.scope: Connection and protocol metadata from traffic visible to the sensor.

providers.name: Suricata EVE
providers.scope: Configured flow, alert, DNS, HTTP, TLS and protocol records.

configuration: Use an authorized lab TAP/SPAN, virtual mirror or gateway interface. Define which traffic crosses it; avoid assuming visibility into every segment.
Enable the required Zeek analyzers or Suricata EVE event types. Export logs with sensor identity, clock synchronization and flow correlation identifiers.
Monitor capture loss, truncation and exporter sampling. Capture payload only with approval and restrictive retention; encryption normally prevents plaintext inspection.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Flows are not packet payloads. NAT, asymmetric routes, encryption, missing mirrors and sampling can hide attribution or content. A destination connection alone does not prove malicious intent.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per source and observation point: connection rate, destination-host/port fan-out, response/failure ratio and previously unseen destinations. Compare equivalent time windows; separate authorized scanners, NAT and sampling effects.

analytics.name: Analytic 1860
analytics.guidance: Real-time network monitoring identifies a source issuing read-only Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol requests to multiple field devices at a polling rate exceeding the legitimate Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) baseline, from a source not in the approved control server allowlist. Because the action is read-only, source-identity and rate deviation are the only available distinguishing signals. OT operational-fidelity gate: Do not alert on novelty, scan/read volume, or enumeration alone. Alert when the source role is not authorized for discovery/polling and the target scope, address/tag range, protocol, or rate deviates from the established operational baseline. Suppress normal SCADA/HMI/historian polling, commissioning, asset inventory, backup, diagnostics, and approved engineering activity.

tuning.description: Allowlist of OPC client application identities authorized to connect.
IP allowlist of legitimate SCADA/HMI/historian servers authorized to poll field devices.
Measured normal polling frequency per device, derived from actual baseline traffic capture.
Documented register/tag address ranges that legitimate SCADA polling actually queries.

software.name: Stuxnet
software.description: [Stuxnet](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0603) examines fields recorded by the DP_RECV monitor to determine if the target system is in a particular state of operation. (Citation: Nicolas Falliere, Liam O Murchu, Eric Chien February 2011)

references.source_name: Nicolas Falliere, Liam O Murchu, Eric Chien February 2011
references.description: Nicolas Falliere, Liam O Murchu, Eric Chien 2011, February W32.Stuxnet Dossier (Version 1.4) Retrieved November 17, 2024.

software.name: Industroyer
software.description: [Industroyer](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0604)'s OPC and IEC 61850 protocol modules include the ability to send stVal requests to read the status of operational variables. (Citation: Anton Cherepanov, ESET June 2017)

references.description: Anton Cherepanov, ESET 2017, June 12 Win32/Industroyer: A new threat for industrial control systems Retrieved. 2017/09/15

software.name: Industroyer2
software.description: [Industroyer2](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1072) uses a General Interrogation command to monitor the device’s Information Object Addresses (IOAs) and their IO state values.(Citation: Industroyer2 Forescout July 2022)

references.description: Forescout. (2022, July 14). Industroyer2 and  INCONTROLLER In-depth Technical Analysis of the Most Recent ICS-specific Malware. Retrieved March 30, 2023.

software.name: FrostyGoop
software.description: [FrostyGoop](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1165) can read data from holding registers via Modbus communication.(Citation: Dragos FROSTYGOOP 2024)

references.description: Mark Graham, Carolyn Ahlers, Kyle O'Meara; Dragos. (2024, July). Impact of FrostyGoop ICS Malware on Connected OT Systems. Retrieved November 20, 2024.

mitigations.name: Mitigation Limited or Not Effective
mitigations.description: This type of attack technique cannot be easily mitigated with preventive controls since it is based on the abuse of system features.

simulation.prerequisites: Use a process simulator or isolated test rig with no connection to production controllers or physical actuators. Preserve safety interlocks; destructive effects require synthetic evidence, not real equipment damage.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
